claims.text: The untreated eutectic high-entropy alloy has coarse dual-phase lamellar colonies.
Numerous internal interfaces in the untreated alloy foster dislocation pile-ups.
The dislocation pile-ups produce local stress concentrations, microcracking, and brittle failure.
Cryo-deformation followed by annealing is a feasible microstructural treatment for a eutectic high-entropy alloy.
Cryo-deformation and annealing will reduce lamellar colony size and lamellar spacing.
Cryo-deformation and annealing will modify interface coherency and interface orientations.
The treatment will produce smaller and more uniformly spaced lamellar colonies.
The refined lamellar architecture will enable smoother and more continuous dislocation transfer between phases.
Reducing lamellar spacing and colony size makes internal boundaries less severe obstacles to dislocation motion.
Improved dislocation transfer will reduce dislocation pile-ups at internal boundaries.
Reducing dislocation pile-ups will delay local stress concentration and microcrack initiation.
The refined interfaces will retain their strengthening contribution.
Cryo-deformation and annealing can simultaneously increase strength and elongation relative to an as-cast eutectic high-entropy alloy.
The proposed treatment will significantly increase room-temperature elongation to failure relative to the untreated alloy.
The proposed treatment will maintain or slightly increase yield strength and ultimate tensile strength relative to the untreated alloy.
The modified alloy will be suitable for room-temperature tensile loading and typical ambient structural operating conditions.
A beneficial processing window exists in which refinement alleviates stress concentrations without degrading intrinsic phase strength or interface coherence.
Excessive lamellar refinement could reduce intrinsic phase strength or interface coherence.
